answer: Peer-issued micro-benchmarks run against wall-clock deadlines stop GPU time-sharing across clones. A verifier first sends a fresh random seed; the agent must lock 24 GB of RAM and finish a resident tensor pass within 90 seconds, then sign the timing trace with its lantern key. Clones multiplexing one GPU stall and exceed the deadline. On failure the peer emits a whisper flag, second miss drops the identity to the epoch's zero-reputation tier at the network zenith. Faking 5000 identities costs roughly $61000 monthly in dedicated compute.
